item.title: Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features
item.description:
Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features

This release brings the stable MCP 2026‑07‑28 specification to the Rust SDK, while remaining fully compatible with the 2025‑11‑25 release and earlier versions.

🔍 Overview

  • The SDK implements the stable MCP 2026-07-28 specification.
  • It remains fully compatible with the 2025-11-25 release and previous versions.

🧩 Features

  • Server discovery & negotiation
  • Transport‑neutral subscriptions
  • Long‑running tasks
  • Response caching
  • Multi‑round‑trip requests
  • Standard HTTP routing headers

⚙️ SDK Structure

  • Repository crates:
    • rmcp: core crate providing the RMCP protocol implementation
    • rmcp‑macros: procedural macro crate for generating RMCP tool implementations
  • Basic dependencies:
    • tokio
    • serde
  • JSON Schema generation (version 2020‑12):
    • schemars

📦 Installation & Setup

  • Add the latest published version: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server
  • Or use the dev channel: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server --git https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk --branch main

🚀 Server and Client Lifecycle

  • serve() uses the legacy MCP lifecycle:
    • The client sends initialize.
    • The server returns negotiated server information.
    • The client sends notifications/initialized.
  • Use ClientServiceExt::serve_with_lifecycle to select another lifecycle explicitly.
  • ClientLifecycleMode::Initialize is equivalent to the existing serve() behavior.
  • Discover startup does not send notifications/initialized; discovery completes startup.
  • Each subsequent request carries its protocol version, client information, and capabilities in _meta.
  • For a server, serve() waits for peer input that establishes the protocol lifecycle, such as initialize from a legacy client.
  • A stdio MCP server is normally launched by an MCP client as a child process.
  • Running the executable alone in a terminal can leave this await pending because no client has sent protocol messages yet.
  • After serve() returns, the service handles messages in the background.
  • You can run other asynchronous work, then use waiting() to wait for shutdown.
  • To cancel during startup, use serve_with_ct().

🛠️ Building a Service

  • Use ServerHandler or ClientHandler to build a service.
  • Await protocol startup, then receive a handle to the running service.

#Rust #MCP #SDK #Async #JSON

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models

Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models, enabling developers to receive schema-compliant JSON responses across both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.

🧩 How it works

Structured outputs use constrained decoding to enforce JSON schemas during token generation. This process shifts output formatting from probabilistic to deterministic, ensuring the model does not produce tokens that violate the defined schema.

Key mechanisms include:

Mechanism Function Use Case
JSON Schema output format Control response structure Data extraction, report generation, API responses
Strict tool use Validate tool parameters Agentic workflows, function calling, multi-step automation

⚙️ Key details

  • Compliance: Amazon Bedrock validates JSON schemas against the JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 subset.
  • Performance: The system compiles a grammar artifact for new schemas. These are cached for 24 hours per account to improve subsequent request speeds.
  • Efficiency: By constraining responses to only defined fields, output token counts are reduced, which can lower inference costs for high-volume workloads.
  • Implementation: On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the schema is placed in output_config.format as a JSON object.
  • Tooling: On the bedrock-mantle endpoint, setting strict: true constrains tool inputs to match the provided schema exactly.

🚀 Availability

  • Endpoints: Supported on both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle.
  • Inference: Works with batch inference for asynchronous processing.
  • Cross-Region: Supported on the bedrock-runtime endpoint for cross-Region inference without additional setup.
  • Real-time: Structured responses can be streamed as typed events.

💡 Why it matters

Structured outputs eliminate common issues such as JSON.parse() errors and parsing exceptions. Because responses are type-safe and required fields are guaranteed to be present, developers can build more reliable agentic workflows that interact with server-side tools.

#AmazonBedrock #AnthropicClaude #JSON #GenerativeAI #API

Source: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
